Synopsis:
An attempt to talk to a gondian worker. The player may recieve information about the kidnapped families in the iron throne.

Cluster Contexts:
- LOW_SteelWatchFoundry_GondianWorker01.json: The scene takes place in the Steel Watch Foundry after the player has confronted Banites/Iron Throne forces; the NPC is a Gondian worker (Lowa in these examples) who was coerced into labor under overseers and may still be traumatized or collared. Depending on prior play, Gondians can be terrified and still working, shaken after fighting overseers, reacting to the Iron Throne exploding, or isolated if leaders like Toobin or Barchus are dead — some workers may also have helped kill Banites and now fear consequences. In the samples Lowa is panicked and repeatedly cries “they’re dead,” meaning her kidnapped family held by the Iron Throne, though a player might misinterpret that as referring to dead guards. The player’s earlier actions (whether they attacked the Iron Throne, freed the foundry, or killed Banites) shape what information Lowa will give about the kidnapped families and how she responds to comfort or provocation.
- LOW_SteelWatchFoundry_Confrontation_AfterIRN.json: This dialog plays if the player solves the Iron Throne before ever seeing the LOW_SteelWatchFoundry_DeadMansSwitchThreat dialog.After destroying the Iron Throne the player walks in Baneites tormenting Gondian Workers in the Foundry Work room.With the Iron Throne gone, the dead mans switch no longer works.
- LOW_SteelWatchFoundry_GondianWorker_PostIRN01.json: This node plays after the player returns from the Iron Throne with at least two workroom gondians dead; the deaths and the Iron Throne raid happened off‑screen. Lilly Tilly is a frightened workroom gondian who helped the player kill Banites but now fears reprisals from the Overseers and regrets fighting back. She remains physically and mentally bound by the collars that control the gondians and expects punishment or execution for the revolt. The wider consequences of the Iron Throne/Gortash encounters (and related rescue/prison events) may have set this up, but those specifics happen off‑screen.
- LOW_SteelWatchFoundry_Dead_DeadGondian.json: The player speaks with a dead gondian who was beaten to death by Banites for knowing too much.
- IRN_IronThrone_ReturnHostages.json: The hostage thanks the player for saving him and/or the other hostages. He will also beg the player to save their families working in the Steelwatch Foundry, giving them the quest if they don't already have it. If the majority of Iron Throne hostages AND the majority of Steelwatch Foundry hostages are saved, they will aid the player by making Steel Watchers on their side for the final battle. Otherwise they won't.Some variation based on whether the player has already been to the Steelwatch foundry and knows about the Iron Throne hostages, promised to help free the Iron Throne hostages, or doesn't know anything about them.If enough Iron Throne hostages survived, they should hint the player that they might reward them if they save their families. If not enough Iron Throne hostages survived, they should make it clear that the player will not receive any signifacant reward, other than narrative and thanks.If EscapedHostage has died, the dialog will trigger by talking to any one of the other surviving Gondians, but a Narrator will talk instead of all of them, as otherwise the permutations are too many. This will be an edge case, as EscapedHostage is very very likely to survive.

context: The scene takes place in the Steel Watch Foundry after the player has confronted Iron Throne/Banite forces; the NPC is a Gondian worker (Lowa in the examples) who was coerced into labor and may still be collared, traumatized, or shaking from recent violence. Off‑screen events include the Iron Throne’s actions against Gondian families (who were kidnapped and held by the Iron Throne) and the player’s prior raid or fights there, which determine what Lowa will say and how she reacts. In the samples Lowa is panicked and repeatedly cries “they’re dead” — she means her kidnapped family back with the Iron Throne, though the player might initially think she’s referring to dead guards. Some Gondians helped fight the Banites and now fear reprisals, and if the Iron Throne was destroyed the foundry’s dead‑man switch is no longer a threat.
